overview:
California's 38th District, redrawn to lean Democratic by about eight points, will elect a new representative this year. Hilda Solis, a former congresswoman and Los Angeles County supervisor, enters as the heavy favorite, having raised roughly $1.4 million with no reported outside opposition spending. Republican Pedro Casas has reported no fundraising, leaving him badly outmatched in resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate profiles, and money. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. The combination of a favorable map, a well-known nominee, and a large financial edge points to a comfortable Democratic margin in the high teens to low twenties, though the absence of polling leaves some room for surprise.
